en: The technique is conducted under the guidance of categories previously stabilized in the theoretical path, with attention to the formation and communication of promises, to the conditions of enjoyment and permanence, to mechanisms of unilateral modulation, to sanctioning practices and to persistent losses that reconfigure the link between promise and delivery. Bias control derives from the archived record of the material used, from limiting the weight of narratives and from triangulation with primary documentation and legal material, so as to reduce selective confirmation and to keep the analysis bound to observable elements. The scope of the procedure is to describe verifiable institutional patterns and mechanisms, without any claim to measure the statistical prevalence of individual experiences or to infer the supplier's psychological intentions.

As a result, situated institutional observation produces traceable descriptions of platform governance at the level of enjoyment, capable of making intelligible typical mechanisms of promise, expectation and delivery, mutability of conditions, curation, programmed scarcity, sanction and normalization of loss. These descriptions and references anchor, in a controllable manner, the use of illustrative vignettes throughout the theoretical-dogmatic path, preparing the later return to parameters of verifiability, control of abusiveness and restoration, without depending on isolated episodes and without any claim to empirical saturation.

Empirical collection includes a targeted documentary analysis of the supplier's terms of use, licenses and internal policies, understood as institutional instruments that structure enjoyment and govern the permanence of the relationship in continuous digital services. The set of documents actually mobilized in the text is selected for its pertinence to the problem investigated and serves to capture the declared norm of the ecosystem, that is, the repertoire of promises, duties, unilateral powers and enforcement procedures presented as a <1>p. 64</1> condition of access and use. In platform-governed objects, such instruments do not operate as mere informational accessories, for they take part in configuring the content of the supply over time and delimit, explicitly or implicitly, the range of permitted modulations, the sanctioning regimes and the mechanisms of challenge and restoration.

The documentary <1>corpus</1> analyzed consists, as a rule, of the versions in force and publicly accessible during the period in which the writing was closed, taking the month of March 2026 as the temporal reference. The investigation is not oriented toward an exhaustive historical reconstruction of earlier versions, nor toward the systematic indexing of contractual changes over time. Past versions and relevant changes will be considered only exceptionally, when there is a verifiable public record attributable to the supplier, such as official announcements, patch notes, institutional history pages or equivalent materials, and when such an element is necessary to qualify a legally relevant modulation of the promise, of the sanctioning regime or of restoration.

For methodological purposes, the primary institutional documents included are those officially attributable to the supplier and intended to guide the use of the service, internal governance and the performance of the relationship. Depending on their pertinence to the problem investigated, this set includes terms of use and general conditions, licensing instruments and authorizations of use, conduct and integrity policies, rules on penalties and moderation, refund and chargeback policies, policies on updates and changes to features, security and anti-fraud rules, as well as policies and notices that affect the form of access and permanence. Official support and communication materials may also be incorporated, with complementary status, such as help pages, institutional FAQs, announcements and public statements by the supplier, when they function as relevant statements of promise, of procedure or of the institutional justification offered to the user.

The reading of the documents is guided by categories stabilized in the theoretical path and by analytical axes oriented toward decidability. Instead of a full exegesis of each instrument, normatively relevant elements are extracted in a targeted way to reconstruct, over the course of the relationship, (i) the ways in which the object and the performance are qualified, (ii) the powers of unilateral modification and their triggers, (iii) the forms of institutional justification and of risk allocation, and (iv) the promises of compensation, refund and restoration. In this sense, the aim is to identify how the service is described and promised, how access is structured and conditioned, which limits of use are set, which rules of conduct organize belonging, which mechanisms of sanction and restriction are provided for, which channels of challenge and review are offered, which refund and restoration regimes are <1>p. 65</1> declared and which informational duties are provided for in situations of change, punishment or restriction. This extraction makes it possible to reconstruct the formal design of the relationship and to locate the points at which the platform converts governance into continuous enforcement, especially when the performance is reconfigured by rule changes, updates and unilateral interventions on access and on the internal conditions of enjoyment.

In the case of computer programs, documentary extraction will also be conducted in a targeted way, seeking (i) references to the period of technical validity of the version marketed, update cycles, discontinuation milestones and conditions for withdrawal from circulation; and (ii) the design and effectiveness of the channels for support, maintenance and provision of complementary technical services. These elements speak directly to specific legal duties of the sector, notably the requirement of a clear indication of the period of technical validity in the license contract and related documents (Law No. 9,609/1998, Art. 7) and the obligation to ensure, during that period, complementary technical services relating to the proper functioning of the program, considering its specifications, even in the event of withdrawal from commercial circulation, subject to compensation for losses possibly caused to third parties (Law No. 9,609/1998, Art. 8).

The documentary survey is treated under an internal hierarchy, so as to avoid undue equivalences between types of institutional instrument. Terms of use, licenses and penalty and conduct policies are taken as the primary normative core of the governance regime, because they structure powers, duties and consequences. Support materials, help pages and official announcements are mobilized with complementary status, capable of evidencing public promises, declared procedures and justifications offered to the user, without replacing the normative core when the analysis depends on definitions of formal powers, of sanctioning regimes or of risk allocation. This distinction is relevant to keep under control the passage from the document to dogmatic attribution, preventing auxiliary communications from being treated as equivalent, in authority and stability, to the central normative instruments of the ecosystem itself.

Since terms and policies in continuous digital services may be modified over time, documentary temporality is handled in a controlled manner compatible with the scope of the corpus. The documents actually mobilized are collected and preserved in the state in which they appeared at the moment of capture, with a record of context and of minimum traceability metadata, so as to allow reconstruction of what was declared in the version used. When earlier changes are pertinent to the argument, they enter only occasionally and with verifiable public support, avoiding <1>p. 66</1> any suggestion of a broad historical reconstruction and preserving coherence between the material cited and the empirical moment to which the analysis refers.

Documentary analysis operates in coordination with the situated institutional observation described above. While observation makes it possible to reconstruct the norm in operation at the level of enjoyment, the reading of terms and policies captures the declared norm and makes explicit the formal repertoire of powers, duties and procedures that sustains private governance. Triangulation between these planes makes it possible to identify convergences and frictions between formal promise and practical enforcement, especially in sensitive matters such as unilateral modification, sanctions, account restrictions and restoration, providing a verifiable basis for the institutional reading of contractual governance throughout the path and for the later dogmatic conversion into parameters of control of abusiveness, verifiability and protection.

The scope of the procedure is to delimit, with traceability, the declared institutional design of the ecosystem, without claiming that documents, by themselves, prove the concrete way in which the rules are applied day to day. The central utility of the documentary corpus is to provide a normative-practical map of the powers and promises that structure continuous enjoyment, allowing the empirical analysis and the dogmatic reconstruction to operate on verifiable and intersubjectively controllable bases, consistent with the methodological purpose of making consumer conflicts in regimes of platform governance decidable.

The survey of public statements by users is part of empirical collection with a delimited and subsidiary purpose, as a symptomatic record of recurring frictions in the ecosystem. Its objective is to observe how controversies associated with platform-governed enjoyment emerge and circulate publicly, which losses are perceived and narrated, which expectations are stated as frustrated promises and which mechanisms of sanction, restriction or modulation appear as recurring triggers of conflict. This material is not mobilized as autonomous proof of the supplier's institutional conduct, nor as a substitute for official documents, interface records, lawsuits or decisions. It is used to map recurring frictions, to identify relevant vocabularies and discursive patterns and to guide triangulation with the declared norm and with the norm in operation, under minimum selection and recording criteria that allow external verification of the material actually cited.

In this design, the verifiability of what is stated about promises, sanctions, procedures and restoration is sought primarily through documentation attributable to the <1>p. 67</1> supplier, public records and traceable statements, without presupposing the building of a broad image archive of the interface. Thus, accounts, complaints and videos may operate, as the case may be, as a record of publicly perceived frictions and as useful vignettes for formulating hypotheses and testing, in an illustrative key, the robustness of the proposed categories. When, however, the argument depends on a specific institutional attribution, such as the content of an internal rule, a sanction criterion, a binding promise or a restoration procedure, the support rests on traceable and attributable sources, with public narratives used only as a starting point for locating verifiable elements.

Community and platform sources, such as forums, social networks, collaborative repositories and creators' content, are treated with a delimited and subsidiary methodological function. They are not mobilized to establish, by themselves, the content of the supplier's internal policies, its decision criteria, its moderation procedures or the existence of obligations assumed, nor to assert the occurrence of disputed institutional practices. Their usefulness is restricted to contextualizing publicly perceived controversies, to identifying recurring vocabularies and practices in the ecosystem and to locating verifiable leads that guide the search for primary documentation. Whenever the analysis depends on normatively relevant elements, priority is given to terms, policies, announcements, support materials and documentary records directly attributable to the supplier.

When mobilized, these sources are treated as a record of public perception and as a means of locating events and documents, and not as an autonomous basis for institutional attribution, so that their argumentative weight always remains subordinate to primary sources or to publicly verifiable elements.

The selection of public statements focuses on two main arenas, chosen because they function as recurring channels for publicizing conflicts in the ecosystem: YouTube, as a space for accounts and controversies in audiovisual format, and structured complaint platforms that record consumer conflicts in the user's language under thematic classification. On YouTube, priority is given to materials that address legally relevant problems for the object and that contain a verifiable reference to an event, change, sanction, account restriction, loss of items/benefits, charge, support or institutional procedure, with a record of the minimum metadata and, when necessary, a timestamp of the pertinent excerpt. For complaints, screening favors those with a sufficient description of the conflict, an indication of the request for restoration and elements that make it possible to relate the narrated friction to a promise, condition of use, support procedure, challenge or governance mechanism of the service.

<1>p. 68</1> The study of public statements on YouTube is justified because it is a central space for publicizing controversies in the ecosystem, with narratives that frequently reconstruct events, point to documents and make explicit the perceived impacts on enjoyment. The interest is not to evaluate "opinions" as such, but to observe how certain conflicts become publicly knowable, which elements are mobilized as justification and which promises, losses and restorations appear in the language of the field.

The primary unit of treatment, on the axis of public statements, is the video, understood as a closed piece with traceable metadata. Internal segments are treated as an autonomous unit only when they reproduce inaccessible external material, crystallized as a quoted excerpt, in which case segmentation preserves the verifiability of the apud. Comments do not constitute an independent corpus and enter only when indispensable to understand, correct or complete the content of the video itself.

The analysis of public statements was conducted through a coding matrix oriented toward categories capable of translating the discursive material into elements relevant to the reconstructed legal problem. In both arenas, at a minimum, the following are observed: the type of problem narrated, the affective reaction and the tone of the account, the perception of loss and the elements of the supply that the user considers affected, as well as the promises and expectations mobilized, whether by explicit reference to advertising, to features, to internal conditions of enjoyment, to support and challenge procedures, or by a statement of what would be owed in terms of adequacy and restoration.

To maintain control, selection favors videos that address legally relevant problems for the object and that allow anchoring by traceable reference, with a record of the minimum metadata and, when necessary, of the point in time at which the relevant excerpt occurs. Comments are collected only when indispensable to understand the video itself, such as corrections, factual additions, retractions, updates or direct indication of public documents.

To prevent the research from expanding indefinitely as an effect of the hyperconnectivity typical of the field, the survey is limited by a non-expansion rule. External sources enter only when they are (a) official, (b) necessary to make explicit the minimum technical functioning of the object, or (c) expressly referred to by an item already included. The unit of treatment for audiovisual statements is always the video, with its own record sheet, and a "segment" is admitted only in the case of an apud record, that is, when an excerpt of an inaccessible external document or external video is crystallized within an included video.

<1>p. 69</1> Reddit is part of the research design as a complementary source because of the relevance of that space for community discussions and, in some cases, for the circulation of public statements and records that help reconstruct the chain of events. Its use is conditioned by the volatility of the environment, in which content may be moderated, removed or reorganized without notice.

For this reason, Reddit is mobilized in a referenced manner, preferably on the basis of mentions and links contained in videos or in documents already included, avoiding an infinite drift of the field. Its use does not serve to infer the representativeness of opinions or the prevalence of events, but to locate chains of events, terms of reference and verifiable leads when the public environment of the ecosystem makes them relevant. The incorporation of Reddit content into the text is exceptional and subject to two limitations: it is used only when indispensable to the argument and, when used, the excerpt is presented with sufficient context to preserve the meaning of its post, avoiding undue identification of non-public users.

To enrich the technical-operational intelligibility of terms, internal structures and vocabulary of the field, and only as a complement to official sources, collaborative repositories such as Fandom are used subsidiarily. This material is used for the strict purpose of naming categories of the ecosystem, describing mechanics operationally and, as an aid, reconstructing basic relations between elements of the service when this is indispensable to translate their functioning into legally intelligible language. Because it is a collaborative environment subject to variation, its content is not used to prove institutional promises, internal decision criteria, official milestones of change or duties assumed by the supplier. When information found there is relevant to the argument, it operates as a lead for locating primary documentation or verifiable public records.

This survey is articulated with the other empirical fronts provided for in the methodology section and remains subject to cross-checking of sources. Public statements are treated as qualified indications and as verifiable leads to locate points of friction and to guide the search for primary material, without converting accounts into direct proof of the supplier's internal policies or procedures. Whenever the analysis requires institutional attribution, such as statements about rules, sanction criteria, formal moderation practices, binding promises or restoration procedures, priority goes to official documents and interface records, compared additionally, when pertinent, with the findings of the minimum institutional analysis of the disputed norm. This preserves coherence between the <1>p. 70</1> subsidiary function of this survey and the dogmatic purpose of the path, which is to make consumer conflicts in continuous services under platform governance decidable.

Every item actually mobilized in the text is recorded with minimum traceability metadata (platform, author, channel or profile when public, title, URL, publication date when available and access date). The traceability of the complaints and textual statements cited is ensured according to the defined recording standard, prioritizing the indication of metadata that allow them to be located on the original platforms. Audiovisual materials are not archived in full. When mobilized, their verifiability is ensured by a complete reference and, when pertinent, a timestamp of the cited excerpt and a transcription of the relevant excerpt in the body of the text or in an explanatory note, without prejudice to the preservation of full copies of the documentary items cited for purposes of auditing the path. The protocol aims to reduce the volatility effects typical of platforms and to maintain the auditability of the path without converting the survey into an exhaustive inventory or imposing the creation and maintenance of a media archive.

As to argumentative weight, the material operates as support for intelligibility and as a source of vignettes, without replacing, when specific institutional attribution is necessary, the support in primary sources and publicly verifiable records.

The <1>Riot Games</1> ecosystem, centered on <2>League of Legends</2>, was selected for the density and diversity of the public traces it produces. The continuous operation of the service, the repeated administration of identity and reputation and the institutional presence of the game as a <3>p. 60</3> platform of participation generate abundant and heterogeneous empirical material, with user statements, records of conflicts and technical-normative documentation circulating in multiple layers. This availability is not treated as a mere convenience, but as a methodological condition for articulating evidence on promises, relevant losses and mechanisms of private governance, in proportion to the argumentative weight of each statement, preventing the case from being reconstructed only on the basis of official terms or only on the basis of narratives of experience.

To preserve proportionality between documentation effort and argumentative weight, a distinction is drawn between three layers of information mobilized throughout the work. The first comprises elements of general knowledge widely disseminated in the sector, used only to situate the reader and make the logic of continuous digital services intelligible, without any claim to prove a specific occurrence. The second comprises auxiliary technical-operational descriptions, used to name internal structures and to understand the vocabulary of the field, with subsidiary support from collaborative repositories when indispensable. In this layer, public narratives may be mobilized as illustrative scenarios to formulate hypotheses and test the applicability of the proposed categories, without any claim to specific institutional attribution. The third comprises normatively relevant statements, such as institutional promises, powers of modulation, sanction criteria, challenge procedures and restoration parameters, which are supported, whenever mobilized as a premise of legal qualification, by traceable and attributable sources, with priority given to the supplier's primary documentation and to verifiable public records.

Empirical collection is organized by a controlled inductive-deductive movement. It starts from categories previously stabilized in the theoretical path to guide the reading of the material and, at the same time, admits that empirical frictions may require refinement of those categories, without converting empirical work into an inventory or into statistical sampling. The material actually mobilized in the text is organized into three families of sources, with distinct and complementary functions: (i) official documents and communications of <1>Riot Games</1>; (ii) public video statements by users and content producers, above all on <2>YouTube</2>; (iii) community discussions referred to by such statements, with priority for threads retrieved on <3>Reddit</3> when there is a direct reference, and analyses by the specialized media and press when they serve as a historical and conceptual record relevant to the analysis. The general rule is to work by triangulation and sufficiency of the core of evidence pertinent to the argument, rather than pursuing exhaustiveness or representativeness.

<1>p. 61</1> The company's official and public documentation is part of the research survey as a structural source for reconstructing the private governance regime of the ecosystem, including terms, policies, public communications and institutional materials relevant to understanding promises, internal rules of permanence and forms of sanction. The dogmatic and bibliographic analysis, in turn, is not treated as an “empirical source”, but as a lens of interpretation that organizes what counts as evidence, what counts as a promise and what counts as a relevant loss in the regime of the Immaterial Object of Consumption. To preserve the fluidity of the central text, only the level of description necessary to make the path auditable will be kept in the body of the section. The methodology used and the justification for the choice of theoretical framework will be duly set out and discussed, when pertinent, in their respective development sections.

The empirical references mobilized in the work are kept traceable by precise indication of origin and access date, with priority for stable public records. In the case of public content subject to change, traceability is ensured by a minimum record of the item's identifier, the source address and the consultation date, without any claim to constitute an exhaustive repository of full captures.

The objective is to reduce the volatility effects typical of digital environments, such as later changes, removals, blocks and reorganizations, preserving the content as it was available at the moment of collection. Preservation focuses on the textual and documentary material actually mobilized in support of the argument, while interface records and references to visual elements are included only if strictly indispensable to understanding the mechanism described and to the minimum verifiability of the point being made.

The three families of sources are detailed in the following subsections, organized by methodological strand. The strand of situated institutional observation (2.4.1) describes the norm in operation at the level of enjoyment. The strand of documentary analysis (2.4.2) captures the declared norm and the institutional design of the relationship. The strand of public statements (2.4.3) records the plane of social perception of frictions, losses and frustrated expectations, with a subsidiary function disciplined by the hierarchy described in the preceding paragraphs.

The institutional reading of the contract, in this work, starts from the recognition that terms of use and internal policies do not operate as static instruments for declaring intent, but as parts of a governance apparatus that integrates rule, implementation and continuous enforcement. In platform-governed ecosystems, the relevant promise is not exhausted in the contractual text, because it is reiterated and recalibrated by interface, reward routines, scarcity regimes and private sanctions. Even so, the contract remains legally central, since it is there that licenses, delimitations of access, unilateral powers and modulation clauses that sustain the enclosure and administration of the relationship are articulated. The procedure adopted consists of articulating the formal instruments with evidence of institutional functioning in order to bring the case back to the categories of the regime of the Immaterial Object of Consumption and make it legally decidable.

With the aim of making explicit how the materials consulted are organized and read to anchor the dogmatic reconstruction developed throughout the thesis, it is stated at the outset that the purpose is neither to describe the ecosystem as a factual narrative, nor to constitute an autonomous demonstrative <1>corpus</1> <2>p. 71</2>. The aim is to stabilize a controllable inferential path that makes it possible to qualify promise, delivery, loss and restoration in continuous digital services whose enjoyment depends on platform governance. Within this frame, the reference to the case operates as a <3>locus</3> of exemplification, used sparingly and with minimum traceability when necessary, to make relevant mechanisms visible without the field material becoming a substitute for the dogmatic foundation.

The contractual analysis takes as its reference, as a rule, the versions in force and accessible during the period in which the writing was closed (March 2026), with specific consideration of past changes only when there is a verifiable public record and when this is necessary to qualify a legally relevant modulation of the relationship.

The analysis articulates three planes as dimensions of the same phenomenon, without any claim to describe the case for its own sake or to validate it by <1>corpus</1>. First, an internal documentary-normative plane, composed of terms of use, policies and official support documents, in which one observes how the platform qualifies the object, defines licenses and enclosures, reserves unilateral powers and presents justifications and promises of compensation. Second, a technical-semiological plane, in which one observes how interface, metrics, visibility regimes and reward systems convert signs into value and into everyday discipline, producing operational dependencies and expectations. Third, a public experiential plane, derived from open statements, in which one observes recurring patterns of friction, perception of loss and invocation of institutional promises and procedures. These planes function as a bridge of intelligibility to anchor, in a verifiable manner, the dogmatic reconstruction.

The articulation between these planes is conducted by categories previously stabilized in the theoretical-normative scope, to prevent the material from being read as a collection of isolated cases or as loose rhetorical illustration. Public statements, observation of interfaces and <1>marketing</1> materials are read in light of semiotic vulnerability and of mechanisms of anticipation and steering by signs, so as to make intelligible how belonging, reputation, time and recognition form part of the promise and value of what is acquired. Contractual documents and judicial decisions are read in light of the qualification of the IOC as an immaterial product in a consumer relationship, of abusive teleology as a criterion for controlling architecture and governance, and of the parameters of open auditability and functional value equivalence as keys for dealing with opacity and mutability without neutralizing protection. The function of this procedure is to discipline the use of references, ensuring that they serve the intelligibility and contestability of the argument, without claiming for themselves the status of exhaustive empirical demonstration.

<1>p. 72</1> The reference to interpretation according to contractual complexity is mobilized here as a methodological instrument for reading terms of use, internal policies and related documents as an institutional technology for governing consumption, and not as a neutral expression of private autonomy. In continuous digital services, complexity is not merely textual length. It is an indication of the distribution of normativity across layers, with reservations of power, sanction patterns and restoration mechanisms that come to form part of the very infrastructure of what is acquired. Within this frame, interpreting the contract means reconstructing the regime it organizes, including when practical performance takes place through interface, support routines and unilateral decisions applied over time.

For this reason, an interpretive technique is adopted that is compatible with highly complex contracts and with asymmetric supply contexts, in which the form of the contract and the institutional environment in which it operates are relevant elements for reconstructing essential content, legitimate expectations and typical zones of abusiveness. Complexity, here, is treated neither as a moral defect of the contract nor as a virtue in itself. It is treated as a legal sign of a supply regime that concentrates decision-making power, disperses information, makes comparability difficult and shifts the conflict to the continuous performance of the relationship.

Within this frame, the reference to Posner, Eggleston and Zeckhauser is strictly instrumental. Their perspective authorizes treating the form of the contract as an indication of the institutional environment in which it operates interpretive questions about essential content, legitimate expectations and typical zones of abusiveness in standardized and unilaterally structured contracts <1>Zeckhauser</1><2>(Posner; Eggleston; Zeckhauser, 2000, p. 92)</2>. This interpretive key serves to prevent terms of use from being interpreted as self-sufficient text and to justify reconstructing the regime on the basis of evidence of how the service functions, without replacing the dogmatic parameters of the CDC.

With the adoption of this perspective, contractual complexity functions as a roadmap for qualifying the relationship, guiding the identification of zones of informational asymmetry, of possible structural advantages and of external factors relevant to the practical functioning of the contract, above all when the logic of use of these instruments is unilaterally established by hegemonic actors <1>Zeckhauser</1><2>(Posner; Eggleston; Zeckhauser, 2000, p. 92)</2>. This key does not replace the dogmatic parameters of the Consumer Protection Code, but acts as a methodological bridge that authorizes describing the phenomenon with sufficient rigor to support the theoretical reconstruction and the dogmatic conversion of the regime.

<1>p. 73</1> This caveat does not alter the control parameter, which remains dogmatic and protective, but describes a practical condition of reading in contracts that function as a governance interface and not as a complete photograph of the relationship.

Converging with this caution, Macaulay indicates that contracts, in various situations, operate less as an ordinary mechanism for resolving conflicts and more as a tool for self-planning, whose activation tends to occur as an <1>ultima</1> <2>ratio</2> <3>Macaulay</3><4>(Macaulay, 1963, p. 55)</4>. For interpretive purposes, this recommends favoring the factual situation and the conflict actually manifested, rather than presupposing that the text fully describes the relationship and its concrete expectations <5>Macaulay</5><6>(Macaulay, 1963, p. 61)</6>.

In the context of continuous digital services, this caveat reinforces the treatment of terms of use as part of a broader institutional regime, in which the practical performance of the relationship takes place through interface, support and sanction routines, requiring a reading connected to evidence of how the service functions. The orientation preserves affinity with the values of objective good faith and with the protective teleology of the Consumer Protection Code, without shifting the axis of legal control to an abstract trust in the contractual text <1>Macaulay</1><2>(Macaulay, 1963, p. 55; p. 61)</2>.

The reading of the legal phenomenon of platforms refuses the artificial separation between norm, technique and culture. In the platform economy, governance is not exhausted in the written rule. It is also exercised through choice architecture, interface design, brand language, curation of affects and continuous symbolic production. Updates, events, campaigns, characters, <1>slogans</1> and performances do not surround the object investigated as mere ambience. They form part of its mode of operation. It is in this context that the curation of epigraphs enters the method, as a way of apprehending, in an artistic and culturally situated register, tensions constitutive of contemporary digital consumption, among them anxiety, desire for belonging, disorientation, euphoria, frustration, capture and performative compulsion.

The epigraphs appear neither as ornament, nor as an authority substituting for the scientific method, nor as empirical proof of the argument. Their function lies elsewhere. They condense, in public and traceable artifacts, the affective and semiotic structure surrounding the consumer relationship in digital environments. When drawn from the very business ecosystem taken as an illustrative reference, they do not count as an institutional confession or endorsement <1>p. 74</1> by the supplier, but as a public inscription of the symbolic universe in which enjoyment, trust and permanence come to be administered through language, aesthetics and performance.

The epigraph opens the section, sets its atmosphere and circumscribes the environment of experience in which the legal problem will be addressed. The analytical work of the section comes afterwards. The argument is not founded on the excerpt, nor does it draw its chain of validation from it. What is preserved, with its presence, is the perception that the phenomenon investigated does not fit entirely into the technical-normative language with which Law usually describes it. In a thesis that deals with platforms as structures for steering conduct, retaining relationships and administering meanings, ignoring the aesthetic thickness of the object in the name of a supposed rigor would only impoverish it.

Nor does the epigraphic curation import into the text the full content of the songs, nor does it presume total coincidence between the artistic work and the problem investigated. The procedure is selective. It cuts specific excerpts, repositions passages, makes deliberate omissions and, when necessary, adjusts punctuation to preserve the meaning of the excerpt in the new context, at times incorporating emphases present in the vocal performance and not in the usual transcription. It is not a matter of summarizing the work, but of assembling, with methodological discipline, an expressive core relevant to the reading of the section.

Art, in different traditions, has served as a public device for guiding reading, preparing the gaze and conducting memory. In archaic Greek literature, the invocation of the Muses, as in Hesiod<1><2>24</2></1>, organizes the account, delimits its tone and situates the voice that speaks. The presence of nine epigraphs emulates the nine Muses and reinforces the framing character of the resource. Each section is opened by a culturally situated lens that precedes the argumentative development. In a dramatic key, the function also approaches that of the chorus, not because the text wishes to theatricalize its object, but because it recognizes that certain conflicts require, beyond conceptual formulation, a voice that keeps their moral and affective atmosphere in circulation.

<1>p. 75</1> The resource also approaches, within a disciplined scope, the lineages gathered in the field of <2>Law and Humanities</2>. In “Law and Literature”, “Law and Film” and “Law and Art”, the cultural work does not replace legal analysis, but expands its capacity for reading<3><4>25</4></3> by placing Law again before experiences that formalism tends to reduce<5><6>26</6></5>. This approach matters here for a precise reason: digital consumption regulated by platforms is not merely an obligational relationship mediated by technology, since it is also a regime of perception, belonging, promise, reward, threat, visibility and opacity. Legal language, when it insists on describing it only as contract, performance or functionality, runs the risk of getting its very object wrong.

There is also a function of denaturalization that is decisive for this thesis. By bringing legal discourse closer to the symbolic universe actually inhabited by the consumer, mechanisms of power that formalism tends to leave out of the frame become more visible. A relevant part of the regulation exercised by platforms is not carried out through explicit normative statements, but through signals, stimuli, settings, metrics, rewards, frictions and interaction scripts. This is private power exercised also on the semiotic plane, in which narrative, aesthetics and design take part in shaping vulnerability and, in certain cases, the very materiality of the unlawful act. Cultural curation helps expose the concrete texture of what Law must learn to name in order to be able to control it.

<1>p. 76</1> As regards the historical-cultural delimitation of the repertoire mobilized, it is worth noting that the meaning attributed by the songwriter herself to <2>The Fear</2><3><4>27</4></3>, the general epigraph of the work, originated as a diagnosis of an inaugural moment of digital life, the one in which a “performed self” begins to be demanded and in which the liberating promise of the networks begins to reveal, almost immediately, its face of continuous exposure, falsity and capture. The most expressive fact lies precisely in the gap between the moment of composition and the later maturation of the technical ecosystem she intuited. What had emerged in a satirical key became literal. The song already recorded, in a still embryonic state, the public fabrication of versions of oneself, the anxiety for validation and the diffuse feeling of submission to a regime of appearances that would later merely consolidate.

It is along this itinerary that <1>The Love Club</1>, the second general epigraph and the opening of the introductory section, introduces the problem of the attraction exercised by digital communities and of the loneliness produced by closed belongings, in which entry into an ecosystem exacts, little by little, a withdrawal from external reality. The following section is received by <2>Birds of Prey</2>, which states the predatory face of the contemporary economic system by portraying an environment in which surveillance and extraction convert enjoyment into hunting ground. In the fourth section, Oh No! condenses the semiotic and psychopolitical capture of the achievement-subject, imprisoned between the obsession with metrified success, the mechanization of conduct and the paradoxical submission to one's own digital assets and possessions. The fifth section closes this block through a dialogue between Scarlet Envy's performance and the lyrics of <3>Villain</3>. The joint composition no longer merely insinuates, but personifies governance by architecture in its most assertive form, by portraying a regime in which unilateral control and manipulation of affects appear as the constitutive logic of its functioning.

In the case of <1>Villain</1>, an additional element of special methodological relevance stands out. Produced by <2>Riot Games</2> itself as part of the artistic universe of the ecosystem taken here as an illustrative reference, the composition describes, in the first person and in the language of entertainment, a power structure founded on unilateral command, affective instrumentalization, disposal of the other and deliberate absence of empathy. The ecosystem, in narrating itself culturally, projects an intelligible image of its own regime of power, and it is this <3>p. 77</3> self-descriptive gesture, not a legal confession, that matters to the argument. A <4>Lex </4> <5>Plataformae</5> does not govern only by contract, code and interface. It also governs by plot, style, character and performance. When the business universe converts into a consumable cultural product a narrative compatible with the type of rationality the thesis seeks to qualify critically, this convergence forms part of the intelligibility of the phenomenon.

The alternation between English-language and Brazilian compositions is not contingent either. The English-language block records the global grammar of digital consumption in its promises of belonging, in its incentives to self-exploitation, in its normalization of capture and in its diffuse regime of opacity. The Brazilian block, in turn, signals the return to the institutional ground of national Law and the passage from the experience of the problem to the formulation of the response. The transition between languages is not a lateral aesthetic detail. It stages the central passage of the thesis itself. The problem emerges on a global scale, within private platform architectures. Legal containment, however, is built with national instruments, under the constitutional order and the Consumer Protection Code.

For this reason, opening the methodological section, <1>Coisas Que Eu Sei</1> marks the passage from the affective and cultural universe of the problem to the legal horizon of intelligibility and control. From there on, the Brazilian epigraphs accompany the progressive formulation of the dogmatic response. In the sixth section, <2>Diz Nos Meus Olhos (Inclemência)</2> expresses the violence of the expropriation of time, existential investment and subjective continuity accumulated under administered relationships.

Next, for the seventh section, <1>Infinito Particular</1> stages the confrontation with the technical black box and, by rejecting illegibility as destiny, mirrors the demand for open auditability. <2>Temporal</2>, in turn, closes the path by translating, for the eighth and last development section, the disorientation of the subject facing the loss of self-recognition under conditions of semiotic vulnerability and identity captivity. In the plea for a “fermata that can now make time obey me”, the concluding image of the epigraphic method emerges: the demand for a legal regime capable of interrupting technical arbitrariness and of subjecting the temporality of supply to criteria of stability, integrity and controllability compatible with the constitutional economic order and with the CDC.

Seen together, the epigraphs thus build a narrative arc parallel to the argumentative arc of the thesis. Each chapter opening condenses, in artistic language, the specific movement that the dogmatic development will carry out in legal language. There is direction, structure and progression. The sequence of the nine epigraphs travels, in a symbolic key, <1>p. 78</1> the same passage that the thesis travels in a dogmatic key: from the finding of the problem to its legal containment, from capture to institutional response, from fear to the fermata.

There is, further, an effect that deserves precise naming. In a thesis whose central category is semiotic vulnerability, the recourse to epigraphs not only accompanies the argument but proposes to confirm it performatively, since it demonstrates, through the very medium of signs, that the symbolic plane is not peripheral, but constitutive of the phenomenon investigated. Contemporary popular culture captured the experience of digital capture before dogmatics had a vocabulary fine enough to name it. Lily Allen recorded the fear of being programmed to consume. MARINA staged self-exploitation as identity. Pitty formulated, under the image of the fermata, the desire to interrupt a temporality that has ceased to obey the subject.

That these signs are themselves products of the culture industry, and not the spontaneous expression of those who consume them, does not weaken the argument, but confirms it: it is precisely when the symbolic commodity becomes the language in which the subject feels, desires and suffers that semiotic capture becomes observable. Such records reveal that the social experience of capture already circulates as a recognizable form of suffering, estrangement and loss before its legal formulation. A study of governance by signs that refused, even in its framing, the signs actually inhabited by the consumer would not be more rigorous. It would merely be myopic.

For this reason, what the epigraphs accomplish, in the end, is not limited to accompanying the text with cultural repertoire. They sustain, in a second voice, a demonstration decisive for this thesis: that the consumer's experience under platforms is semiotically constituted, and that the relevant injury in these environments cannot be satisfactorily apprehended when Law insists on speaking a language foreign to the one in which consumption actually takes place. The symbolic register precedes the argument, frames it and intensifies it, announcing, with the means proper to art, the passage from symptom to response, in which national Law is called upon to give back, in the form of protection, what the global private regime tends to normalize as loss and to leave without appropriate legal nomenclature.

Hesiod, a Greek poet associated with the archaic period, composes in the <1>Theogonía</1> a poem of genealogical organization of the divine, in which the origins of the cosmos and the succession of powers and lineages culminating in the Olympian order are narrated. The work functions as a narrative map of the world, gathering traditions and stabilizing a public memory about where the gods come from, how authority is structured and why certain hierarchies prevail. It is in this frame that the nine Muses appear, daughters of Zeus and <2>Mnemosyne</2> (Memory), as a figuration of inspiration and, above all, of the capacity to give form to the true account as the transmission of what must be remembered. The invocation of the Muses, in this context, is not devotional ornament, but a protocol of enunciation, marking that the account is mediated by a symbolic source of intelligibility, organizing the discourse and legitimizing the enunciative gesture. As a formal detail, the numerical coincidence between the nine Muses and the nine epigraphs of the work helps make explicit, without any claim to equivalence of status, the function of the epigraphs as narrative frame and key of interpretive orientation. <3>↩</3>

The mobilization of cultural repertoires as interpretive support does not constitute ornament and approaches the field of <1>Law and Humanities</1> as described by Maria Paola Mittica <2>(2015, p. 25)</2>, Doctor in Sociology and Associate Professor at the <3>Università degli Studi di Urbino</3>, who proposes a structural distinction between <4>Law and Humanities</4>, “Law and Literature” and “Law and Music”, in which the first functions as “genus” and the others as “species”, alongside other cuts such as “Law and Film” and “Law and Art”. In this frame, the dialogue with the humanities does not shift the axis of validation of the argument to the aesthetic plane, since the methodological proposal is precisely to promote a controlled exchange between specialized competences, oriented toward building analytical instruments adequate to the object. Mittica summarizes the question by stating that, in <5>Law </5> <6>and Humanities</6>, “a research methodology is assumed that is intended to promote dialogue between different specialized competences” <7>Mittica</7><8>(Mittica, 2015, p. 25)</8>. Thus, the epigraphic use can be understood as a hermeneutic frame and a symptomatic record of the symbolic field, without needing to enter the evidentiary chain or replace dogmatic description, qualification and critique. <9>↩</9>

In this sense, André Karam Trindade, Associate Professor in the Graduate Program in Law of the Centro Universitário de Cascavel (UNIVEL), refers to José Calvo González to reinforce that the use of cultural artifacts can operate as an auxiliary instrument for reading the legal phenomenon without becoming empirical proof or citation of authority. Trindade observes that, in the field of the arts, Calvo González wrote on relations between <1>Law and Cinema, Music, Iconography, Photography</1> and other expressions so as to demonstrate that the dialogue between Law and artistic expressions can be methodologically fertile without reducing the legal to the aesthetic (Trindade, 2021, p. 86). Moreover, in characterizing the idea of a <2>Literary Culture of the Law</2> as a two-way street, his text makes explicit that the gain lies not in “proving with art”, but in expanding intelligibility, vocabulary and perception of layers of experience that technical-normative language tends to impoverish. This two-way street is formulated on the basis of two dimensions, the literary reading of law and the legal reading of literature (Trindade, 2021, p. 106). The methodological consequence is compatible with the proposed epigraphic device, since the epigraph functions as a frame and reading support for the symbolic field, while the argument is sustained by dogmatic and institutional analysis, without the cultural repertoire forming part of the grounding as an inferential premise. <3>↩</3>

In an interview with the British newspaper <1>The Telegraph</1> in 2018, Lily Allen revisited the original meaning of the song and the proportion such phenomena assumed over the following years: “It’s funny, because when I wrote it, it was meant to be quite tongue-in-cheek and sarcastic, but it’s become quite literal now, sadly. I was spending a lot of time on MySpace and I guess just starting to know Twitter and it felt like people were putting across a version of themselves that wasn’t necessarily ‘true’. In its infancy, social media felt liberating. And then it felt, quite immediately, quite false. I think ‘The Fear’ was my reaction to those falsehoods.” (Allen <2>apud</2> Vicent, 2018) <3>↩</3>

The methodological design centers on a paradigmatic case, the <1>Riot </1> <2>Games</2> ecosystem with <3>League of Legends</3>, in its <4>desktop </4>and <5>mobile </5>(“<6>Wild Rift</6>”) versions, within a defined time frame and relying on public and documentary sources, so as to build a verifiable <7>p. 79</7> <8>corpus</8>. This choice limits the mapping of variations by type of platform, by national market and by technological generation, and is not aimed at producing statistical inferences from a representative sample. The extended case study works with a different logic, since it favors the case's contribution to theoretical reconstruction and to the identification of mechanisms, rather than its quantitative representativeness. Consequently, the kind of generalization sought is analytical, not sample-based.

These limits are addressed through a disciplined scope and through triangulation. Reliance on public materials is accepted as a condition for the external verifiability of the path, with explicit criteria for inclusion in and exclusion from the research <1>corpus</1>, with the recording and preservation of the material actually used and with cross-references to organizational appendices. The researcher's position in the field does not operate as a criterion of proof, but as a sensitivity that detects reading hypotheses, which remain subject to testing against institutional documentation and traceable records, so as to prevent frictions and controversies from being treated as anecdote.

The work's potential for generalization derives, first, from what the instrumental empirical laboratory makes observable, not from anything “typical” or “individual” about the case, and it yields analytical generalization through mechanisms and relevant frictions. For this reason, this work does not offer a reflection on <1>League of Legends</1> as an isolated cultural object, but on the regime of the immaterial object of consumption it contains and on the techniques of private governance used by the continuous digital services that sustain it, reconstructed with the support of an ecosystem that lays bare dependence, modulation of access, internal sanctions, an economy of virtual items and the semiotic management of enjoyment.

Second, the transposability of the proposed regime is treated as a complementary methodological stage, through illustrative applications and tests of fit of the keys developed, in typical contemporary situations of continuous digital consumption, designed to make recurring functional equivalences and evidentiary requirements visible without turning the path into an extended case study or an exhaustive empirical demonstration.

In this key, the conclusions are transposable when other environments share equivalent structural mechanisms, such as games under the <1>games-as-a-service</1> model, <2>marketplace </2>and <3>gig economy</3> platforms marked by layers of reputation and conditional access, and account-based content-mediation and artificial intelligence services with unilateral rules and continuous adjustments to the offer. Transposition does not proceed by superficial analogy, but by identifying functional equivalences between governance architectures, forms of <4>p. 80</4> enforcement and patterns of friction, which makes it possible to carry the IOC regime over to other cases without turning the research into a sectoral thesis on a single product.

In keeping with this discipline of methodological transparency, it should also be noted that, throughout the writing and revision, artificial intelligence systems were used as support tools for organizing the text, comparing formulations and detecting inconsistencies in the argument. The use of these tools does not replace research, does not alter the criterion of proof and does not produce interpretive authority. Their function is to assist in revising the text and controlling its quality. Substantive decisions, including scope, selection of sources, legal qualification, structure of the argument and final wording, remain entirely the author's responsibility.

Danni Carlos, <1>Coisas Que Eu Sei</1> (2008). <2>What it announces</2> · <3>Read the epigraph in the PDF</3>.

In platform economies, power tends to disguise itself as technical administration while it concentrates knowledge, organizes attention and redefines the conditions of participation. The central methodological risk, with an object of this kind, is to let the apparent neutrality of how things work stand in for an analysis of how private decisions produce practical norms and distribute asymmetries. For this reason, the work starts from a political warning that serves as the horizon of the problem: when knowledge is concentrated and everyone else is pushed into irrelevance, the answer is not contemplation, it is critical capacity and human quality.

<1>El mundo se va a ir dividiendo [...] en los irrelevantes y los dueños de conocimiento </1> <2>[...]. Si nos quedamos de brazos cruzados no vamos a servir ni para que nos exploten </2> <3>[...]. Entonces se necesita una sociedad muy inteligente, muy capacitada [...]. Como </3> <4>seres humanos, no hemos evolucionado tanto como evolucionó la tecnología. Por eso </4> <5>hay que pelear por [...] mejorar la calidad humana. Eso se llama cultura, </5> <6>conocimiento y ejemplo. No me quiten la utopia.</6> (MUJICA..., 2023<7><8>15</8></7>)<9> </9>

It is on this foundation that the methodology adopted here presents itself as a legitimate taking of position, refusing to naturalize “how the platform works” as if it were a neutral method, marked by the absence of choice, and treating governance by architecture as a full phenomenon, and therefore one that can be legally described and reconstructed in dogmatic terms. The methodology represents a position toward the kind of power observed in platform economies and, therefore, toward the kind of temptation such an object creates for the researcher. In environments in which private administration and the management of conduct present themselves as technical neutrality, the central analytical risk is to naturalize decisions as if they were mere “functioning”, to reduce institutional choices to “operational details” and to attribute to the user, as autonomy, responses that have already been induced by design, communication and mechanisms of incentive, disincentive and sanction. The methodological design therefore takes as a premise that the regime under which the service actually operates emerges from the coupling of clauses, interface and institutional practices, which precludes readings that artificially separate norm, technique and culture.

The research strategy organizes collection and analysis procedures capable of reconstructing, in a controllable way, how promises are formed, how expectations become stable and how <1>p. 46</1> relevant losses arise in continuous relationships. The aim is to preserve the legal intelligibility of the phenomenon without reducing its social density, since the exercise of authority in the ecosystem is distributed among contractual instruments, interface architectures and enforcement routines. The methodological consequence is a triangulation that makes it possible to trace inferences back to traceable evidence and to keep the object legally decidable, avoiding both abstraction cut off from practice and description that abdicates normative qualification.

This stance explains the choice to combine theoretical-dogmatic reconstruction with an instrumental empirical laboratory and with controlled exemplification, complementing this anchoring with illustrative applications and tests of fit of the proposed keys in typical situations of continuous digital consumption. In relationships of this nature, in which conduct and expectations are administered through proprietary signs and institutional routines, the user's concrete experience is no longer external noise and becomes part of the very regulatory mechanism to be understood. This proximity does not authorize psychologizing, nor does it turn familiarity with the field into a criterion of proof. It serves to guide the gaze toward observable mechanisms of promise, friction and sanction, which must then be anchored in traceable and publicly verifiable evidence.

To keep the inferential path controllable, the literature drawn on throughout the work is handled through a methodological distinction between object and instruments<1><2>16</2></1> <3>Eco</3><4>(Eco, 2007, p. 69)</4>. The object is the regime of platform-governed enjoyment and its mechanisms of promise, expectation, modulation and sanction. The instruments are the conceptual keys used to qualify this regime in language suited to the application of norms, which makes it possible to convert phenomena of architecture, communication and technical execution into operational categories compatible with legal duties, limits and consequences. In practical terms, frameworks from political economy, sociology, philosophy, the anthropology of consumption and communication theory come in to guide the identification of relevant mechanisms and to discipline inferences, without requiring an exegetical reconstruction of the works drawn on, so that the argument <5>p. 47</5> can still be traced back to traceable evidence and to recognizable normative parameters <6>Eco</6><7>(Eco, 2007, p. 69-70)</7>. This distinction aims to prevent both exegetical drift and the merely ornamental use of concepts.

In this key, the choice of a non-exegetical approach does not work as a shortcut, but as a conscious delimitation of focus. When a concept is used as a tool to read an object other than the one in which it was formed, the interest lies in what it makes visible in the observed field and in how it improves the legal intelligibility of the problem, without requiring a philological reconstruction of its origin, of internal debates and of the concept's historical variants in its home domain, except where indispensable to avoid significant distortion.

The disciplined scope finds explicit support in Umberto Eco <1>(2007, p. 70-71)</1>, who distinguishes the study of a body of thought at its origin from the study of its later uses and appropriations, and points out that, in certain cuts, what matters is what was made of the concept<2><3>17</3></2>. In methodological terms, this guidance allows the full genealogy of a concept to be treated as a topic only when it is needed to prevent distortion, and not as a mandatory stage of every instrumental use.

This chapter gathers the elements needed to make the investigation auditable, including the research strategy, the empirical scope and the techniques for collecting and reading the material used. This sets a standard of transparency and control capable of tracking the chain linking evidence, categories and inferences throughout the work. It thus preserves the argumentative continuity of the following sections, in which the analysis concentrates on the theoretical and dogmatic dimensions of the problem.
Excerpt from an interview given by former Uruguayan President José Alberto “Pepe” Mujica Cordano to DW Brasil <1>source</1><2>(MUJICA..., 2023)</2>. <3>↩</3>

Eco treats the distinction between the object of research and the instruments used to make it intelligible as an organizing premise of intellectual work and as a check against turning auxiliary texts into a subject of exegesis. “A thesis studies an object using certain instruments. Often the object is a book and the instruments are other books. This is the case, for example, of a thesis on The economic thought of Adam Smith, whose object consists of the books of Adam Smith, while the instruments are other books about Adam Smith. […] In other cases, on the contrary, the object is a real phenomenon; this is what happens with theses on internal migratory movements in present-day Italy, on the behavior of a group of disabled children or on public opinion about a television program currently on the air.” <1>Eco</1><2>(Eco, 2007, p. 69)</2>. Methodologically, Eco's remark supports the view that interdisciplinary literature can operate as an instrument for qualifying the observed phenomenon without requiring an exegetical reconstruction of the works used when they are not the object of the investigation. <3>↩</3>

Eco offers an express formulation to justify cuts that seek not a full philological reconstruction of a body of thought at its origin, but the examination of its uses and appropriations in another context, provided the objective is clearly delimited. He gives an example: “It could, however, be a case in which the original thought interested me very little. Let us suppose I began a thesis on Zen thought in the Japanese tradition. […] Suppose, however, that, in examining the critical literature, I became interested in the use a certain American literary and artistic avant-garde made of Zen in the 1950s. Evidently, at this point I am no longer interested in knowing with absolute theological and philological exactness what the meaning of Zen thought would be, but rather in knowing how ideas originating in the East became elements of a Western artistic ideology. […] Assuming, of course, that I do not intend to show that the Californians misunderstood the original Zen, which would make comparison with the Japanese texts mandatory. But if I limit myself to presupposing that they drew freely on translations from the Japanese, what interests me is what they made of Zen and not what Zen was at its origin.” <1>Eco</1><2>(Eco, 2007, p. 70-71)</2>. The example makes explicit that the requirement to return to origins depends on the problem formulated and on the kind of claim one intends to support. <3>↩</3>
